summary: Unit tests in AuthServiceTest are strong: meaningful StepVerifier assertions, behavior-focused, every TDD anchor for AuthService is covered with state checks (Redis INCR/EXPIRE, session TTL via ArgumentCaptor, eventService.logEvent params, WebSession.invalidate). TokenServiceTest and EventServiceTest are clean. AuthControllerIT, however, is a @WebFluxTest slice — not a real Testcontainer-backed IT — and four of the six TDD-anchor IT tests are not implemented (sessionFixation_newSessionId, rememberMe_sessionTtlIs30Days, noRememberMe_sessionTtlIs24H, loginSuccessEventInDB). Two further gaps: AuthService.me() branch logic has no unit test (only a controller slice with the service mocked), and Decision 4 fail-open Redis behavior is unverified. Mock count in AuthServiceTest is 5 + per-test WebSession/exchange mocks, which is the test-pyramid trade-off the task explicitly acknowledged (AbstractIntegrationTest deferred). The deferral is fine but is not documented in AuthControllerIT.

findings.issue: Four of the six TDD-anchor integration tests listed in tasks/4.md are missing: login_success_sessionFixation_newSessionId, login_rememberMe_sessionTtlIs30Days, login_noRememberMe_sessionTtlIs24H, login_success_loginSuccessEventInDB. The current file is a @WebFluxTest slice with AuthService mocked — it cannot assert on real session IDs, MongoDB sessions.maxInactiveInterval, or events collection contents because there is no real session store, no MongoDB, and no real AuthService running. Acceptance criteria 'rememberMe=true → sessions.maxInactiveInterval >= 2592000' and 'login_success event logged in events collection' are therefore not verified end-to-end anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Two acceptable paths: (a) Add a TODO comment at the top of AuthControllerIT explicitly stating 'True integration tests for session fixation, rememberMe TTL, and events.collection assertions are deferred until AbstractIntegrationTest is created in Task <N>. The session-fixation and TTL behavior is partially covered at unit level in AuthServiceTest::login_success_invalidatesPreAuthSession_andSetsRememberMeTtl and login_success_noRememberMe_setsTtl24Hours.' and update task-4 decisions.md noting the deferral. (b) Write a minimal local AbstractIT stub now using @SpringBootTest + Testcontainers MongoDB+Redis (deps already in build.gradle per Task 1) and implement the four anchors. Path (a) is consistent with the task hint; path (b) closes the gap immediately. If choosing (a), the 4 deferred tests must be added to a task-8 (AbstractIntegrationTest setup) backlog or to task-7's tracking list — otherwise they will silently disappear.

findings.issue: AuthService.me() has 4 branches (no security context, isAuthenticated=false, principal is not AppUserDetails, success), none of which are unit-tested. AuthControllerIT::me_withSession_returns200WithUserBody and me_withoutSession_returns401 mock authService.me() to return canned values, so the actual SecurityContext extraction + AppUserDetails cast + MeResponse mapping is exercised by zero tests. TDD anchor 'me_withValidSession_returnsCurrentUser' is therefore satisfied only at controller-routing level, not at service-logic level.

Decision 4 (Redis is DoS mitigation, not auth gate — fail open) is implemented via three onErrorResume blocks: in checkBruteForce, registerFailure, and resetBruteCounters. None of these branches are tested. If a refactor accidentally turns one of them into an auth-blocking error, no test would catch it. This is a security-relevant invariant.

File is named AuthControllerIT.java and the task labels it as an IT, but it is implemented as a @WebFluxTest slice with @MockitoBean AuthService. This is misleading — the IT suffix in this codebase normally implies @SpringBootTest with Testcontainers. A future contributor reading the file name may assume MongoDB/Redis assertions are inside, find none, and either duplicate the work or skip the gap.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) rename the file to AuthControllerSliceTest.java (or AuthControllerWebFluxTest.java) and create a separate empty AuthControllerIT.java with a TODO stub referencing AbstractIntegrationTest and the 4 deferred TDD anchors, or (b) keep the IT name but add a Javadoc at the class level explicitly stating 'Slice test only. Real Testcontainer-backed IT (session fixation, TTL persistence, events collection) is deferred to Task <N> when AbstractIntegrationTest is created. See work/02-auth/tasks/4.md TDD Anchor list for the deferred tests.'

findings.location: backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/auth/AuthServiceTest.java:50-64 (5 class-level @Mock fields) and lines 202-211, 240-243, 263-270 (per-test WebSession + ServerWebExchange mocks)
findings.issue: AuthServiceTest mocks UserRepository, ReactiveRedisTemplate (with RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS), PasswordEncoder, ServerSecurityContextRepository, EventService — 5 collaborators. Plus each success-path test additionally mocks WebSession × 2 and ServerWebExchange. By the test-master rule (>3 mocks → consider integration test), this is wrong test type. The unit tests still produce value (they are the only place the brute-force/fail-open/dummy-bcrypt logic is verified before AbstractIntegrationTest exists), but the maintenance cost is real — the deep-stubbed redisTemplate.opsForValue() chain is fragile, and stubbing exchange.getSession() to return two different Monos in sequence (line 211, 243, 270) is order-dependent.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as a stopgap given AbstractIntegrationTest deferral. When AbstractIntegrationTest lands (Task 7+), migrate the success-path tests (login_success_invalidatesPreAuthSession_andSetsRememberMeTtl, login_success_noRememberMe_setsTtl24Hours, login_success_resetsBruteForceCountersAndLogsEvent, login_pendingUser_succeedsWithEmailWarning) to integration tests against real WebTestClient + MongoDB sessions collection + events collection. Keep the unit tests for: brute-force threshold checks, dummy-bcrypt timing, fail-open Redis errors, X-Forwarded-For parsing — these remain best at unit level. Add a TODO at AuthServiceTest class-level documenting which tests will move.

findings.issue: Use of @Mock(answer = Answers.RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS) for ReactiveRedisTemplate causes redisTemplate.opsForValue() to return a deep-stub that is reused (not a fresh stub each call) — this is an undocumented Mockito behavior that the test relies on. Verifications such as verify(redisTemplate.opsForValue()).increment(EMAIL_KEY) work because RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS caches the stub. If a future Mockito upgrade changes this caching, all verifications break silently with no failed assertion. Same risk for the verify chain on lines 129-132, 222-224, 250-251, 339-340.

findings.location: backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/auth/AuthServiceTest.java — no test for the 'fallback to remoteAddress when no X-Forwarded-For' branch (AuthService.java:208-218)
findings.issue: extractIp has two branches: XFF present → leftmost IP; XFF absent → remoteAddress.getHostAddress(). Test login_extractsIpFromXForwardedForHeader covers branch 1. Branch 2 (no XFF, fall back to remote) is implicitly covered by all the other tests (which pass remote=10.0.0.7), but no test explicitly asserts 'when XFF absent, the IP key uses remoteAddress'. There is also no test for 'remoteAddress is null' (returns 'unknown') — a defensive branch.

Mock-return anti-pattern (mild form): when(authService.login(...)).thenReturn(Mono.just(response)) and then jsonPath assertions read back the same response fields. Litmus test: if the AuthController.login implementation were replaced with `return authService.login(req, exch).map(ResponseEntity::ok)` (which it already is) or even `return authService.login(req, exch).flatMap(r -> Mono.just(ResponseEntity.ok(r)))`, the test passes either way. The test does verify HTTP wiring (POST /api/auth/login route exists, JSON body is serialized with correct field names, status 200) — so it has some value as a routing/serialization smoke test, but the AuthResponse 'real' contract (status='active', warning=null, etc.) is not verified against a real login flow.
findings.recommendation: Either delete this test (the 401 + 400 tests already verify routing exists, AuthServiceTest covers the AuthResponse construction, and a future real IT will verify end-to-end), or rename it to login_route_serializesAuthResponseAsJson and add a comment 'Verifies controller-level routing and JSON serialization only. End-to-end response contract is verified in <future IT once AbstractIntegrationTest exists>.' Same applies to me_withSession_returns200WithUserBody.

findings.issue: logEvent is fire-and-forget, but two implicit guarantees in AuthService (it ignores the return) are never tested at the EventService boundary: (1) logEvent returning normally even when called rapidly N times in a row, and (2) the event has 'createdAt' set close to Instant.now() — only that it is non-null is checked. These are minor; the persisted-fields test is sufficient for the core contract.
